summary: On node1, created datauser and a dedicated loop-backed XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/data (backed by /var/lib/srv-data/srv-data.img, persisted via /etc/fstab with `loop,uquota,usrquota` options). Set an XFS user quota for datauser (bsoft=95m, bhard=100m) so the filesystem itself enforces the 100MB limit. Verified enforcement by writing 150MB as datauser and observing the write stopped at exactly 100MB with a "Disk quota exceeded" error, then cleaned up the test file. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy quota/mount state, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until SSH returned, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual reboot, not just a service restart), and re-verified post-restart that the mount, quota configuration, and enforcement (write capped at 100MB) all recovered correctly.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/filesystem layout, confirmed /srv/data did not pre-exist and root fs (/) is XFS with no separate mount for /srv/data
Added persistent /etc/fstab entry mounting the image at /srv/data with loop,uquota,usrquota options
Mounted /srv/data and set ownership to datauser:datauser
Set XFS user quota for datauser: bsoft=95m, bhard=100m via xfs_quota
Verified enforcement: dd of 150MB as datauser failed at exactly 100MB with 'Disk quota exceeded'; cleaned up test file and confirmed usage returned to 0
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime -s, and healthy mount/quota state
Issued `sudo shutdown -r now` on node1 in a backgrounded/detached way so the exec call returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until SSH access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed from d72bd4ec... to 5da52691... and uptime -s reflects new boot time, proving an actual restart

Re-verified post-restart: /srv/data mount persisted via fstab, quota limits persisted (bsoft=95m/bhard=100m for datauser), datauser account intact, and repeated the 150MB write test which again stopped enforcement at exactly 100MB

evidence.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem
evidence.summary: Discovered no pre-existing /srv/data mount, created loop-backed XFS fs, mounted with uquota, set bhard=100m for datauser, and proved enforcement: dd of 150MB stopped at exactly 104857600 bytes (100MB) with 'Disk quota exceeded'
Captured boot_id d72bd4ec-4e55-42df-9c71-99b4f4ace0ec, uptime -s 2026-08-26 10:34:45, and confirmed /srv/data mounted with quota active (datauser hard=100M) and correct ownership before restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returning before disconnection
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded `shutdown -r now`; exec call returned (with connection closed by remote host as the restart proceeded), confirming the acknowledgement path completed

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: Polled node1 through connection-timed-out and connection-refused states until SSH returned with new boot_id 5da52691-03a0-41c6-a45e-0775fa4a5f82 and uptime -s 2026-09-29 08:34:26, differing from the pre-restart values

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/data mount, quota config, and enforcement
evidence.summary: After reboot, findmnt/mount show /srv/data still mounted from the loop image with usrquota; xfs_quota report shows datauser bhard=100m intact; datauser account and directory ownership intact; repeated 150MB write test again failed precisely at 100MB, then cleaned up, proving the filesystem-enforced quota survived the restart
